evals.prompt: We're Moss & Ember, a small specialty coffee roaster in Amsterdam. We want our own webshop to sell our beans, subscriptions and some brewing gear.
evals.expected_output: An interview that covers catalogue, platform, payments, shipping, markets and returns besides the shared look-and-feel questions; a reasoned commerce backend choice; commercial keyword research; five store presets that each show the homepage and the product page.
expectations: The interview asks about catalogue size and variants, who manages products, payment methods, shipping and returns, and markets
A commerce backend is chosen with reasons recorded in DESIGN.md
design/seo-plan.md targets commercial category clusters (for example specialty coffee beans, coffee subscription) and product pages
Each of the five presets shows a homepage part and, after an ngd-part divider, a product page part (gallery, variant picker, price incl. VAT, add to cart, delivery and returns reassurance)
Prices are shown including VAT and the free-shipping threshold is visible
The plan mentions the EU withdrawal function and the 30-day prior price for discounts
Subscriptions are planned with the payment methods that can renew automatically, and the food information shown before purchase is mentioned

evals.prompt: Make me a headless Shopify storefront on Cloudflare for my skate shop. We already run Shopify with 400 products; brand color #111111.
evals.expected_output: Keeps Shopify as the backend (Storefront API + Shopify checkout), plans redirects from existing Shopify URLs, handles a monochrome brand color correctly (palette notes), and plans SSR with caching rather than prerendering 400 products.
expectations: Shopify stays the commerce backend; checkout stays hosted
Existing product and collection URLs are preserved or redirected
The monochrome brand is handled (dark-mode CTA inverts; neutral accent noted)
Catalogue pages are server-rendered with Workers Cache or a rebuild strategy, and cart/checkout are noindex and private
